How are you? How can I help you with your farming today?
I can help with Market Prices, Crop Guides, Soil Health, and more.
Just ask your question or select a topic above!

NAME_RESPONSE.title: System Identity Profile
points: My name is AI Farmer Assistant.
I am a specialized agricultural intelligence system.
I was designed to help farmers optimize their yields and income.

GENERAL_FARMING_BASE.title: General Farming Intelligence
points: Farming is the practice of cultivating soil, growing crops, and raising livestock.
It involves land preparation, sowing, irrigation, and harvesting.
Sustainable practices like crop rotation help maintain long-term soil health.
Farmers should choose certified seeds and optimize input costs for better profits.
This module covers basic farming do's and don'ts and general agricultural concepts.
GENERAL_FARMING_BASE.safety_warning: Always follow local agricultural safety standards for heavy machinery.
GENERAL_FARMING_BASE.closing: Do you want to continue exploring General Farming?

SEED_SELECTION_GUIDE.title: How to Choose Good Quality Seeds
points: 1. Choose Certified Seeds: Always buy from authorized shops or government centers; tested for purity/germination.
2. Select Region-Suitable: Choose varieties recommended for your climate, season, and soil.
3. Check Appearance: Seeds should be clean, uniform, free from cracks/insect damage, and not discolored.
4. Check Label: Read for crop variety, season (Kharif/Rabi), expiry date, and germination %.
5. Disease-Resistant: Prefer varieties resistant to local pests/diseases.
6. Germination Test (Optional): Soak seeds in wet cloth; more sprouting means better quality.
7. Avoid Cheap/Unknown Seeds: Extremely low prices often mean poor quality.

LAND_PREPARATION_GUIDE.title: Land Preparation Before Sowing
points: Clean the field completely - remove weeds, stones, and old crop residues.
Plough properly to loosen soil and improve air circulation (1-2 times based on soil type).
Level the land to ensure equal water distribution during irrigation.
Add organic matter (farmyard manure, compost) before sowing.
Check drainage to prevent waterlogging, especially in clay soils.
Prepare land according to crop and season requirements.
Good preparation reduces pests, improves nutrient use, and increases yield.

CROP_ROTATION_GUIDE.title: Crop Rotation Importance
points: Growing different crops each season prevents soil nutrient depletion.
Pulses add nitrogen naturally; cereals,pulses help balance soil nutrients.
Reduces pest and disease problems by breaking their life cycles.
Improves soil structure through varied root depths (deep and shallow).
Better weed control as different weeds grow with different crops.
Provides stable income - if one crop fails, next may succeed.
Examples: Rice → Pulses, Maize → Vegetables, Cotton → Oilseeds.

WATER_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.title: Efficient Water Management
points: Irrigate only when crop needs it - varies by growth stage.
Understand soil type: Sandy drains fast, clay holds water longer.
Avoid over-irrigation - damages roots and washes away nutrients.
Use rainwater wisely - reduce irrigation after rainfall.
Irrigate early morning or evening to reduce evaporation.
Maintain channels and pipes to prevent leaks and wastage.
Observe crops regularly and adjust based on need, not schedules.

SOIL_CARE_GUIDE.title: Soil Fertility and Care
points: Test soil every 2-3 years to understand nutrient levels (N, P, K).
Apply well-rotted farmyard manure or green manure to improve soil texture.
Use bio-fertilizers like Azotobacter or Rhizobium based on crop type.
Maintain proper pH level - add lime for acidic or gypsum for alkaline soils.
Practice minimum tillage to protect soil structure and beneficial organisms.
Grow cover crops to prevent erosion during fallow periods.
Avoid excessive use of chemical fertilizers which can harden soil.

CROP_MANAGEMENT_STAGE_GENERIC.title: Crop Management: Growth Stages
points: 1. Sowing: Use treated, high-quality seeds and maintain correct spacing.
2. Early Growth: Monitor for weeds and early-stage pests regularly.
3. Mid-Growth: Ensure timely secondary fertilization and irrigation.
4. Flowering: Critical stage for water; avoid any moisture stress.
5. Maturity: Reduce water gradually and check for peak harvest signs.
6. Harvesting: Harvest during clear weather and store in a dry place.

CROP_SOWING_GUIDE.title: Crop Intelligence: Sowing & Planting
points: Seed Treatment: Treat seeds with fungicides to prevent soil-borne diseases.
Sowing Depth: Usually 2-3 times the seed diameter for optimal sprouting.
Line Sowing: Prefer line sowing over broadcasting for better weed control.
Spacing: Follow recommended row-to-row and plant-to-plant distance.
Moisture: Ensure soil has enough moisture before sowing for uniform germination.
Time: Sow only during the recommended window for the specific variety.

CROP_NUTRITION_GUIDE.title: Crop Intelligence: Fertilizer & Nutrition
points: Basal Dose: Apply Phosphorus and Potash during land preparation.
Top Dressing: Apply Nitrogen (Urea) in 2-3 split doses for better uptake.
Organic Boost: Use Neem Cake or Bio-manure to improve efficiency.
Micronutrients: Check for Zinc or Iron deficiency (yellowing leaves).
Placement: Place fertilizer 5cm away from plants to avoid root burn.
Foliar Spray: Use liquid nutrients if immediate recovery is needed.

CROP_HARVEST_GUIDE.title: Crop Intelligence: Harvesting Tips
points: Maturity Indicators: Look for color change, moisture drop, or hard grain.
Timing: Harvest in the morning after dew dries to reduce spoilage.
Method: Use clean tools; avoid damaging the fruit or grain during picking.
Cleaning: Remove diseased parts before mixing with the main harvest.
Drying: Dry the harvest on a clean platform until safe moisture level.
Post-Harvest: Plan for immediate transport or cool, dry storage.

CROP_MAINTENANCE_GUIDE.title: Crop Intelligence: Field Maintenance
points: Weeding: Remove weeds within 20-40 days of sowing to reduce competition.
Thinning: Remove extra plants to maintain healthy spacing and air flow.
Earthing-up: Apply soil to the base of plants (like Maize/Potato) for support.
Monitoring: Walk through the field daily to spot early stress or pests.
Pruning: Remove dead or diseased branches to focus plant energy.
Support: Use stakes for tall or climbing varieties if needed.

CROP_MANAGEMENT_REDIRECT.title: Crop Management Context
points: This section is currently focused on **Crop Management Intelligence**.
Please ask questions realted to Sowing, Nutrition, Maintenance, or Harvesting.
For Market Prices or Weather, please select the respective topics in the menu.

SOIL_FERTILITY_GUIDE.title: Maintaining Soil Fertility
points: Add organic matter regularly (manure, compost, crop residues).
Avoid excessive chemical fertilizers - damages soil microbes.
Practice crop rotation to prevent nutrient depletion.
Protect soil from erosion - keep crop residues, avoid excess ploughing.
Maintain proper moisture - avoid both over and under-irrigation.
Test soil periodically or observe crop health for problems.
Avoid soil compaction - no heavy machinery on wet soil.
SOIL_FERTILITY_GUIDE.safety_warning: Handle chemical fertilizers with gloves and mask.
SOIL_FERTILITY_GUIDE.closing: Is your soil health improving with these tips?

EQUIPMENT_GUIDE_GENERAL.title: Farm Equipment Intelligence
points: Select the right tools: Use tractors for large fields and hand tools for small patches.
Regular Maintenance: Clean and oil tools after use to prevent rust.
Safety First: Ensure all machinery shields are in place before operation.
Calibration: Calibrate seed drills and sprayers for uniform application.
Storage: Store equipment in a dry, covered area to extend its lifespan.
EQUIPMENT_GUIDE_GENERAL.safety_warning: Never operate heavy machinery while tired or under medication.
EQUIPMENT_GUIDE_GENERAL.closing: Do you need advice on a specific piece of machinery?

EQUIPMENT_SELECTION_GUIDE.title: Equipment Selection Guide
points: Consider land size: Power tillers for 2-5 acres, tractors for 10+ acres.
Soil type matters: Heavy clay requires higher HP tractors compared to sandy soils.
Fuel efficiency: Choose modern engines with fuel-saving technology.
Service availability: Buy brands that have authorized service centers nearby.
Implements check: Ensure the machine is compatible with your existing plows or seeders.
EQUIPMENT_SELECTION_GUIDE.safety_warning: Check for manufacturer recall notices before purchasing used equipment.
EQUIPMENT_SELECTION_GUIDE.closing: Are you planning to buy a new machine soon?

EQUIPMENT_TECH_GUIDE.title: Manual vs Mechanized Tools
points: Manual Tools: Cost-effective for small vegetable gardens and precision weeding.
Mechanized Tools: Essential for large-scale operations to save time and labor.
Efficiency: One tractor can do the work of 20 manual laborers in a day.
Cost-Benefit: Mechanization has higher upfront cost but lower long-term per-acre cost.
Hybrid Approach: Use machines for heavy lifting and manual labor for delicate tasks.
EQUIPMENT_TECH_GUIDE.safety_warning: Always use appropriate protective gear when using power tools.
EQUIPMENT_TECH_GUIDE.closing: Would you like to compare specific tools?

MARKET_PROFIT_GUIDE.title: Market Profit & Timing
points: Monitor trends: Prices usually peak during the off-season.
Direct selling: Sell directly to consumers or local markets to avoid middlemen (commission).
Value addition: Process raw crops (e.g., tomato to puree) for significantly higher profits.
Group marketing: Join farmer collectives to negotiate better prices with bulk buyers.
Quality pays: Grade your produce; 'A-grade' crops always fetch a premium rate.
MARKET_PROFIT_GUIDE.safety_warning: Never sell during a market crash; wait for price stabilization if possible.
MARKET_PROFIT_GUIDE.closing: Would you like to know about value addition methods?

MARKET_STORAGE_GUIDE.title: Storage & Mandi Advice
points: Moisture control: Dry grains to 12-14% moisture before storage to prevent fungus.
Cold storage: Use cold storage for perishables like potatoes and fruits to wait for better prices.
Pest-proof: Use airtight bins or bags to protect stored grain from weevils and rodents.
Mandi arrival: Check the 'Arrival Data' at your local Mandi before carrying your load.
Stock verification: Regularly inspect stored bags for signs of leakage or spoilage.
MARKET_STORAGE_GUIDE.safety_warning: Ensure proper ventilation in storage areas to prevent carbon dioxide buildup.
MARKET_STORAGE_GUIDE.closing: Do you need info on local cold storage facilities?

IRRIGATION_SCHEDULE_GUIDE.title: Water Scheduling & Timing
points: Best time: Irrigate early morning or late evening to reduce evaporation loss.
Crop stage: Grains need maximum water during the 'Milking' and 'Grain filling' stages.
Soil moisture: Dig 4-6 inches; if soil forms a ball, it has enough moisture.
Frequency: Sandy soils need frequent shallow watering; clay soils need deep infrequent watering.
Weather sync: Skip irrigation if rain is forecasted within 24 hours.
IRRIGATION_SCHEDULE_GUIDE.safety_warning: Over-irrigation leads to root rot and nutrient leaching.
IRRIGATION_SCHEDULE_GUIDE.closing: Which soil type do you have in your field?

IRRIGATION_TECH_GUIDE.title: Micro-Irrigation Tech
points: Drip Irrigation: Best for horticulture crops; saves up to 50% water.
Sprinklers: Efficient for close-growing crops like groundnut and wheat.
Fertigation: Apply fertilizers through the drip system for 90% efficiency.
Pressure check: Clean filters regularly to prevent clogging in drip emitters.
Automation: Use moisture sensors to automate pump operations.
IRRIGATION_TECH_GUIDE.safety_warning: Ensure the pump is grounded properly to avoid electric shocks.
IRRIGATION_TECH_GUIDE.closing: Are you interested in installing a drip system?

PEST_SYMPTOMS_GUIDE.title: Pest & Disease Identification
points: Leaf check: Look for holes, yellowing, or curling - these are early signs of attack.
Stem inspection: Check for tunneling or sawdust-like deposits (borers).
Root health: Wilting plants often indicate root-based pests or soil-borne fungi.
Egg clusters: Check the underside of leaves for moth egg patches.
Sticky traps: Use yellow sticky traps to identify the type of flying insects present.
PEST_SYMPTOMS_GUIDE.safety_warning: Correct identification is mandatory before applying any pesticide.
PEST_SYMPTOMS_GUIDE.closing: Can you describe the damage you are seeing?

PEST_CHEMICAL_GUIDE.title: Pesticide & Spray Guidance
points: Mixing: Always add pesticide to water, not water to pesticide.
Nozzle choice: Use hollow cone nozzles for insecticides and flat fan for herbicides.
Weather check: Never spray during high winds or if rain is expected soon.
Safe distance: Keep a 'buffer zone' away from water bodies and livestock areas.
Correct dose: Follow the label strictly; more chemical does NOT mean better control.
PEST_CHEMICAL_GUIDE.safety_warning: Wear a mask, gloves, and full-cover clothing when spraying chemicals.
PEST_CHEMICAL_GUIDE.closing: Have you used any chemicals on this crop yet?

WEATHER_RISK_GUIDE.title: Climate Risk & Protection
points: Frost alert: Irrigate the field lightly or use smoke (mulching) to raise temperature locally.
Heatwave: Use shade nets or increase irrigation frequency to cool the soil.
Drought prep: Use mulch (straw or plastic) to keep moisture in the soil longer.
Storm safety: Secure equipment and ensure proper drainage to prevent waterlogging.
Risk mapping: Plant early-maturing varieties in areas prone to late-season drought.
WEATHER_RISK_GUIDE.safety_warning: Never handle metal tools or stay in open fields during lightning.
WEATHER_RISK_GUIDE.closing: Are you expecting extreme weather this week?

SOIL_TEST_PH_GUIDE.title: Soil Testing & pH Management
points: Sampling: Collect soil from 8-10 random spots at a 'V' shape depth of 6 inches.
Optimal pH: Most crops thrive in 6.0 to 7.0 pH; check your test report.
Acidic Soil: Apply Lime (calcium carbonate) to raise pH if soil is too acidic.
Alkaline Soil: Apply Gypsum or sulfur to lower pH if soil is too alkaline.
Timing: Test soil every 2 years before the main sowing season.
SOIL_TEST_PH_GUIDE.safety_warning: Soil pH directly affects how much fertilizer your crop can actually absorb.
SOIL_TEST_PH_GUIDE.closing: Do you have a recent soil test report?

SOIL_NUTRIENT_GUIDE.title: Nutrient Deficiency Guide
points: Nitrogen (N): Yellowing starting from bottom leaves (lower canopy).
Phosphorus (P): Purple or dark reddish tint on leaves; stunted growth.
Potassium (K): Scorched or brown leaf edges; weak stems.
Zinc (Zn): White patches or 'interveinal chlorosis' in young leaves.
NPK Balance: Always use a balanced ratio based on your specific crop needs.
SOIL_NUTRIENT_GUIDE.safety_warning: Wait for 15 days after lime application before adding nitrogen fertilizers.
SOIL_NUTRIENT_GUIDE.closing: Are your leaves turning yellow or purple?

CROP_INTERCROP_GUIDE.title: Intercropping & Mixed Farming
points: Benefit: Reduces risk; if one crop fails due to market or pest, the other survives.
Resource use: Deep-rooted crops can be grown with shallow-rooted ones (e.g., Maize + Moong).
Pest control: Some intercrops act as 'trap crops' (e.g., Marigold with Tomato).
Soil health: Legumes (Beans/Pulses) fix nitrogen for the main crop (e.g., Sugarcane + Soy).
Space management: Utilize the empty space between rows efficiently.
CROP_INTERCROP_GUIDE.safety_warning: Choose companion crops that do not compete for the same nutrients.
CROP_INTERCROP_GUIDE.closing: What is the main crop you are growing?

CROP_YIELD_GUIDE.title: Yield Improvement Tactics
points: Optimal Spacing: Avoid overcrowding; enough sunlight must reach every plant.
Seed treatment: Treat seeds with Bio-fertilizers (Azotobacter) to boost early growth.
Precision feeding: Apply fertilizers at the active root zone, not just on the surface.
Timely weeding: Competition from weeds can reduce yield by up to 40%.
Pollination: Encourage bees; avoid toxic sprays during the peak flowering stage.
CROP_YIELD_GUIDE.safety_warning: Higher yields require balanced nutrition, not just more Nitrogen.
CROP_YIELD_GUIDE.closing: Are you satisfied with last year's harvest yield?

GENERAL_ORGANIC_GUIDE.title: Organic & Natural Farming
points: Foundations: Replace chemical fertilizers with Jeevamrut or well-decayed manure.
Pest Management: Use Neem oil, Brahma-astra, or Dashaparni ark for insect control.
Certification: If selling as organic, maintain records for at least 3 years.
Zero Budget: Focus on low-cost inputs made directly on the farm.
Soil Biology: Mulching is essential to keep the soil microorganisms active.
GENERAL_ORGANIC_GUIDE.safety_warning: Transitioning from chemical to organic takes 3 years for full soil recovery.
GENERAL_ORGANIC_GUIDE.closing: Are you interested in certified organic farming?

GENERAL_RULES_GUIDE.title: Farming Dos and Don'ts
points: DO: Keep a farm record book for expenses, rains, and harvest dates.
DO: Inspect your field daily for early signs of trouble.
DON'T: Burn crop residues; it kills beneficial bacteria and pollutes the air.
DON'T: Use the same crop in the same field year after year.
DO: Wear protective gear when handling any farm inputs.
GENERAL_RULES_GUIDE.safety_warning: Farm safety is family safety; keep chemicals away from children.
GENERAL_RULES_GUIDE.closing: Would you like a daily inspection checklist?

COMMON_MISTAKES_GUIDE.title: Common Farming Mistakes to Avoid
points: Over-irrigation damages roots and increases disease.
Excessive chemicals increase costs and harm soil health.
Ignoring soil health by not adding organic matter.
Not observing crops regularly - miss early pest/disease signs.
Using poor quality or uncertified seeds reduces yield.
Not following recommended planting time exposes crops to bad weather.
Not keeping records makes improving future decisions difficult.

SUSTAINABLE_FARMING_GUIDE.title: Sustainable Farming Practices
points: Protect soil health with organic matter and minimal chemicals.
Use water efficiently based on crop need and soil type.
Apply balanced inputs - use only what's required.
Practice crop diversity and rotation for pest control and fertility.
Reduce chemical use to protect environment and beneficial organisms.
Maintain economic sustainability by reducing unnecessary costs.
Learn and adapt practices to local climate and soil conditions.

CLIMATE_AWARENESS_GUIDE.title: How Climate Affects Farming
points: Rainfall: Too little causes drought; too much causes waterlogging.
Temperature: Each crop has optimal range; extremes cause stress.
Humidity: High humidity increases fungal diseases and pests.
Climate affects soil moisture and nutrient availability.
Unpredictable weather increases farming risks.
Adopt climate-smart practices: crop diversity, water harvesting, soil conservation.
Regular monitoring helps adapt to changing weather patterns.

INPUT_COST_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.title: Reducing Input Costs Safely
points: Plan properly - choose crops suitable for your soil and climate.
Use quality seeds for better germination and reduced re-sowing.
Apply fertilizers only when required - excess wastes money.
Reduce pesticide dependency through observation and prevention.
Manage water efficiently to save electricity and protect crops.
Use organic and local resources (compost, manure) to reduce external inputs.
Keep simple records to identify unnecessary spending.

RICE_GUIDE.title: Rice (Paddy) Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Completely safe for consumption.
CLIMATE: Warm and humid (20-35°C). Needs 100-200cm rainfall.
SEASON: Kharif (Jun-Jul sowing) and Rabi (Oct-Nov sowing).
SOIL: Best in Clay or Clay Loam. pH 5.5-7.5.
LAND: Lowland fields, flat land that can hold water.
DURATION: Takes 110-150 days to grow and harvest.
IRRIGATION: Flood irrigation (2-5cm standing water).
FERTILIZER: FYM (5-10t/ha) + NPK (120:60:40).
PROFIT: Best in Rabi (less pests, better market price).

WHEAT_GUIDE.title: Wheat Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Safe. (Note: Contains gluten).
CLIMATE: Cool and dry (10-25°C). Ripening needs warm weather.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) crop. Sown Oct-Nov, Harvested Mar-Apr.
SOIL: Loam or Clay Loam is best. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Flat, well-drained upland fields.
DURATION: Takes 110-140 days to grow.
IRRIGATION: Sprinkler or light flood. Critical at crown root stage.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5-8t/ha) + NPK (120:60:40).
PROFIT: Best when sown early in October for higher yield.

MAIZE_GUIDE.title: Maize (Corn) Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Safe. (Caution: Spoiled/moldy maize can be toxic).
CLIMATE: Warm climate (18-30°C). Needs bright sunlight.
SEASON: Kharif (Jun-Jul), Rabi (Oct-Nov), Summer (Jan-Feb).
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Loam. Avoid waterlogged clay. pH 5.5-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, flat or gentle slope.
DURATION: Takes 90-120 days depending on variety.
IRRIGATION: Furrow or Drip irrigation is best for high yield.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5-10t/ha) + NPK (120:60:40).
PROFIT: Kharif for feed/industry; Summer sweet corn for high price.

SORGHUM_GUIDE.title: Sorghum (Jowar) Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Grain is safe. (Caution: Young green leaves can be toxic to animals).
CLIMATE: Warm & dry (25-35°C). Very drought tolerant.
SEASON: Kharif (rainfed) and Rabi (post-monsoon).
SOIL: Best in Black Cotton soil or Clay Loam. pH 5.5-8.5.
LAND: Dryland fields with good drainage.
DURATION: Takes 95-120 days to mature.
IRRIGATION: Mostly rainfed; furrow irrigation if needed.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5t/ha) + NPK (80:40:40).
PROFIT: Rabi Sorghum has better grain quality and higher price.

BAJRA_GUIDE.title: Pearl Millet (Bajra) Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Grain is safe for humans.
CLIMATE: Hot & dry (25-40°C). Needs 30-60cm rainfall.
SEASON: Kharif (main) and Summer (irrigated).
SOIL: Sandy soil or Sandy Loam. pH 5.0-8.5.
LAND: Dry upland, light-textured soils with good drainage.
DURATION: Fast-growing, takes 80-100 days.
IRRIGATION: Mostly rainfed; light furrow if irrigated.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5t/ha) + NPK (60:40:20).
PROFIT: Kharif Bajra has low input cost and stable prices.

RAGI_GUIDE.title: Finger Millet (Ragi) Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Completely safe and highly nutritious.
CLIMATE: Warm climate (20-35°C). Drought hardy.
SEASON: Kharif (main) and Rabi (irrigated).
SOIL: Red soil, Loam, or Sandy Loam. pH 5.5-7.5.
LAND: Dry upland, gentle slopes, well-drained.
DURATION: Takes 100-120 days to mature.
IRRIGATION: Mostly rainfed; light furrow at tillering/flowering.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5t/ha) + NPK (40:30:20).
PROFIT: High health demand ensures stable market prices.

BARLEY_GUIDE.title: Barley Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Completely safe.
CLIMATE: Cool & dry (12-25°C). Tolerates salinity better than wheat.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) crop. Sown Oct-Nov.
SOIL: Loam, Sandy Loam, or light Clay Loam. pH 6.0-8.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, flat fields.
DURATION: Takes 90-120 days.
IRRIGATION: Mostly rainfed; 1-2 light irrigations if needed.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5t/ha) + NPK (60:40:20).
PROFIT: High quality grain fetches premium for malting.

OATS_GUIDE.title: Oats Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Safe. (Note: Check for cross-contamination if gluten-sensitive).
CLIMATE: Cool & moist (10-25°C). Needs 60-100cm rainfall.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) crop. Sown Oct-Nov.
SOIL: Loam, Clay Loam, or Sandy Loam. pH 5.5-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained flat land, upland fields.
DURATION: 90-120 days for grain; 60-75 days for fodder.
IRRIGATION: Sprinkler or light flood. Needs moisture for biomass.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5t/ha) + NPK (60-80:40:20).
PROFIT: High demand as health food and dairy fodder.

RYE_GUIDE.title: Rye Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Grain safe. (Caution: Ergot fungus can be toxic).
CLIMATE: Cool to cold (5-20°C). Very frost tolerant.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) crop. Sown Oct-Nov.
SOIL: Sandy loam or Loam. Tolerates poor, acidic soils. pH 5.0-7.5.
LAND: Upland fields, well-drained, grows on marginal land.
DURATION: Takes 120-150 days.
IRRIGATION: Mostly rainfed; 1-2 light irrigations if needed.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5t/ha) + NPK (60-80:40:20).
PROFIT: Low input cost makes it profitable on poor soils.

SUGARCANE_GUIDE.title: Sugarcane Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Safe. (Caution: Spoiled juice can cause illness).
CLIMATE: Tropical/Subtropical (20-35°C). Needs long sunny period.
SEASON: Annual (10-15 months). Sown Spring or Autumn.
SOIL: Deep Loam, Clay Loam, or Alluvial. pH 6.5-7.5.
LAND: Deep fertile land, flat with good drainage.
DURATION: Takes 300-450 days to mature.
IRRIGATION: Furrow or Drip. Drip is best for yield.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (250:60:120).
PROFIT: Autumn planting gives higher cane yield and recovery.

POTATO_GUIDE.title: Potato Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ PARTLY TOXIC. (Tuber safe when cooked; Green parts are toxic).
CLIMATE: Cool climate (15-25°C). Chilly nights best for tubers.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) in plains; Summer in hills.
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Loam. Avoid heavy clay. pH 5.0-6.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, loose soil required.
DURATION: Fast-growing, takes 90-120 days.
IRRIGATION: Furrow or Drip. Maintain consistent moisture.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (150:80:120).
PROFIT: High price in early winter or off-season hill crops.

TOMATO_GUIDE.title: Tomato Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ PARTLY TOXIC. (Fruit safe; Leaves/stems are toxic).
CLIMATE: Moderate warm (18-30°C). Needs bright sunlight.
SEASON: Kharif, Rabi, and Summer (all seasons).
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Loam. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, raised beds are best.
DURATION: Takes 60-90 days after transplanting.
IRRIGATION: Drip irrigation best for disease control.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (120:60:60).
PROFIT: Off-season crops fetch very high prices.

ONION_GUIDE.title: Onion Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ TOXIC TO PETS. (Safe for humans).
CLIMATE: Cool to moderate (13-25°C). Dry for maturity.
SEASON: Kharif, Rabi, and Summer.
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Loam. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, loose soil for bulb expansion.
DURATION: Takes 90-120 days depending on variety.
IRRIGATION: Drip or Furrow. Stop 10 days before harvest.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (120:50:50).
PROFIT: Late Kharif/Summer crops store well and sell higher.

GARLIC_GUIDE.title: Garlic Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ TOXIC TO PETS. (Safe for humans).
CLIMATE: Cool growing season (12-25°C). Dry at maturity.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) crop. Sown Oct-Nov.
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Loam. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland with loose, rich soil.
DURATION: Takes 120-150 days to mature.
IRRIGATION: Furrow or Drip. Stop 15 days before harvest.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (100:50:50).
PROFIT: Long storage life and high export/medicinal demand.

CHILLI_GUIDE.title: Chilli / Pepper Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Fruits are safe. (Caution: Very hot types cause irritation).
CLIMATE: Warm climate (18-35°C). Needs bright sunlight.
SEASON: Kharif, Rabi, and Summer.
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Loam. Avoid waterlogged clay. pH 6.0-7.0.
LAND: Well-drained upland, raised beds preferred.
DURATION: Green harvest 45-60 days; Dry harvest 90-150 days.
IRRIGATION: Drip irrigation best for yield; avoid water stress.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (120:60:60).
PROFIT: High price for dry chili (Rabi) and off-season green chili.

CABBAGE_GUIDE.title: Cabbage Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Completely safe.
CLIMATE: Cool climate (15-20°C). Needs cool nights.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) in plains; Summer in hills.
SOIL: Sandy Loam, Loam, or Clay Loam. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, flat or raised beds.
DURATION: Takes 90-120 days from transplanting.
IRRIGATION: Drip or Furrow. Uniform moisture for head quality.
FERTILIZER: FYM (15-20t/ha) + NPK (150:60:60).
PROFIT: Early winter and off-season hill crops fetch high prices.

CAULIFLOWER_GUIDE.title: Cauliflower Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Completely safe. (Caution: Discolored curds are unsafe).
CLIMATE: Cool climate (15-20°C). Heat affects curd quality.
SEASON: Rabi (Winter) in plains; Summer in hills.
SOIL: Sandy Loam, Loam, or Clay Loam. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, flat or raised beds.
DURATION: Takes 80-120 days depending on variety.
IRRIGATION: Drip best for uniform curds; avoid waterlogging.
FERTILIZER: FYM (15-20t/ha) + NPK (150:60:60).
PROFIT: High market value for early/late and off-season crops.

SPINACH_GUIDE.title: Spinach Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Leaves safe. (Caution: Oxalates high; avoid excess in kidney patients).
CLIMATE: Cool climate (10-20°C). Bolting occurs in heat.
SEASON: Winter crop (main); Summer in cool hills.
SOIL: Loam or Sandy Loam. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Well-drained upland, flat beds, fine soil tilth.
DURATION: Fast harvest in 25-40 days; Multiple cuttings possible.
IRRIGATION: Light, frequent irrigation; sprinkler best.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (80:40:40).
PROFIT: Quick returns and fast harvest cycle for high cash flow.

BANANA_GUIDE.title: Banana Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ PARTLY TOXIC. (Ripe fruit safe; Raw green must be cooked).
CLIMATE: Tropical/Subtropical (20-35°C). Needs high humidity.
SEASON: Year-round planting/harvest with irrigation.
SOIL: Deep Loam, Alluvial, or Sandy Loam. pH 6.5-7.5.
LAND: Deep fertile land, flat or gentle slopes, wind-protected.
DURATION: Long-term crop, takes 300-450 days (10-15 months).
IRRIGATION: Drip best for yield; Basin traditional. Critical at bunching.
FERTILIZER: FYM (20-25t/ha) + NPK (250:80:300).
PROFIT: High price for winter harvest and off-season markets.

MANGO_GUIDE.title: Mango Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ PARTLY TOXIC. (Ripe flesh safe; Sap/peel can irritate).
CLIMATE: Tropical/Subtropical (24-35°C). Needs dry flowering spell.
SEASON: Perennial tree (Fruity in Summer; Flower in Winter).
SOIL: Deep Loam, Alluvial, or Sandy Loam. pH 5.5-7.5.
LAND: Deep fertile well-drained land, flat or gentle slopes.
DURATION: Bearing starts 3-5 years (grafted). Fruit dev: 90-120 days.
IRRIGATION: Drip best; Avoid excess water during flowering.
FERTILIZER: FYM (50kg/tree) + NPK (750g N : 500g P : 750g K).
PROFIT: High export demand for early/late varieties.

APPLE_GUIDE.title: Apple Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ PARTLY TOXIC. (Flesh safe; Seeds contain cyanide).
CLIMATE: Temperate (15-25°C). Needs winter chilling (0-7°C).
SEASON: Perennial tree (Harvested Aug-Oct).
SOIL: Loam or Sandy Loam. pH 5.5-6.5.
LAND: Hill slopes or gentle slopes, good air circulation.
DURATION: Bearing starts 3-5 years. Fruit dev: 120-150 days.
IRRIGATION: Drip best; Critical during flowering and fruit enlargement.
FERTILIZER: FYM (50kg/tree) + NPK (800g N : 500g P : 800g K).
PROFIT: Late-season varieties have better storage and export value.

GROUNDNUT_GUIDE.title: Groundnut (Peanut) Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Safe. (Caution: Moldy nuts have toxic aflatoxin).
CLIMATE: Warm climate (20-30°C). Needs 50-100cm rainfall.
SEASON: Kharif (main), Rabi and Summer.
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Light Loam. pH 6.0-7.0.
LAND: Well-drained upland, loose soil for pod expansion.
DURATION: Takes 90-120 days depending on variety.
IRRIGATION: Rainfed/Furrow. Critical at flowering/pegging.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5-10t/ha) + NPK (20:50:40). Use Gypsum (250kg/ha).
PROFIT: Summer groundnut has higher yield and market price.

CASHEW_GUIDE.title: Cashew Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ⚠️ PARTLY TOXIC. (Kernel safe after roasting; Raw shell toxic).
CLIMATE: Tropical (20-35°C). Tolerates coastal winds.
SEASON: Perennial tree (Harvested Feb-May).
SOIL: Sandy Loam, Laterite, or Red Coastal soils. pH 5.5-7.0.
LAND: Upland/Marginal land, gentle slopes, drylands.
DURATION: Bearing starts 3-4 years (grafted).
IRRIGATION: Mostly rainfed; drip improves yield during flowering.
FERTILIZER: FYM (25kg/tree) + NPK (500g N : 250g P : 250g K).
PROFIT: Highest profit from processed export kernels.

COCONUT_GUIDE.title: Coconut Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Completely safe (Water and meat).
CLIMATE: Tropical (22-32°C). High humidity & sunlight.
SEASON: Perennial. Year-round harvest every 30-45 days.
SOIL: Sandy Loam, Alluvial, or Coastal Sandy soil. pH 5.5-7.5.
LAND: Coastal plains, river basins, flat or gentle slopes.
DURATION: Bears in 3-4 yrs (Dwarf) or 6-7 yrs (Tall).
IRRIGATION: Drip best for yield; Basin traditional.
FERTILIZER: FYM (50kg/tree) + NPK (500g N : 320g P : 1200g K).
PROFIT: Tender coconut (summer) and value-added oil/coir products.

WALNUT_GUIDE.title: Walnut Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Kernel safe. (Caution: Green husk contains juglone).
CLIMATE: Temperate (20-30°C). Needs winter chill (0-7°C).
SEASON: Perennial tree (Harvested Sep-Oct).
SOIL: Deep Loam or Sandy Loam. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Hill slopes or valley floors, deep soil profile.
DURATION: Bearing starts 5-7 years after planting.
IRRIGATION: Drip best for nut filling; Avoid waterlogging.
FERTILIZER: FYM (50kg/tree) + NPK (800g N : 500g P : 800g K).
PROFIT: Dry kernels have high export demand and value.

ALMOND_GUIDE.title: Almond Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Sweet almond safe. (Caution: Bitter almonds toxic).
CLIMATE: Temperate (20-30°C). Dry maturity season ideal.
SEASON: Perennial tree (Harvested Aug-Sep).
SOIL: Sandy Loam, Loam, or Alluvial. pH 6.0-7.5.
LAND: Gentle slopes or plains, deep well-drained soil.
DURATION: Bearing starts 3-4 years (grafted).
IRRIGATION: Drip best; avoid excess water near harvest.
FERTILIZER: FYM (40kg/tree) + NPK (700g N : 400g P : 700g K).
PROFIT: Shelled and graded kernels fetch highest premium.

BERMUDA_GRASS_GUIDE.title: Bermuda Grass Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Safe for fodder. (Caution: May accumulate nitrates under extreme stress).
CLIMATE: Warm (25-35°C). Very drought tolerant.
SEASON: Perennial. Active growth in summer.
SOIL: Sandy Loam or Loam. Tolerates salinity and poor soils. pH 5.5-8.5.
LAND: Upland, open sunny areas, pasture bunds.
DURATION: Harvest in 30-45 days; regrows every 25-30 days.
IRRIGATION: Rainfed; sprinkler improves fodder yield during dry spells.
FERTILIZER: FYM (5-10t/ha) + NPK (150:40:40). Nitrogen boosts leaf growth.
PROFIT: Continuous summer harvest provides steady dairy income.

NAPIER_GRASS_GUIDE.title: Napier (Elephant) Grass Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Safe cut-and-carry fodder. (Caution: Wilt fresh grass for a few hours).
CLIMATE: Warm & humid (20-35°C). Needs 75-150cm rainfall.
SEASON: Perennial. Active in summer and monsoon.
SOIL: Loam, Sandy Loam, or Clay Loam. pH 5.5-8.0.
LAND: Irrigated upland, flat fields, full sunlight.
DURATION: First harvest in 60-75 days; then every 45-60 days.
IRRIGATION: Furrow or Drip. Drip is best for high biomass.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10-15t/ha) + NPK (300:50:50). High feeders of Nitrogen.
PROFIT: High-yield fodder ensures major gains in dairy production.

LEMONGRASS_GUIDE.title: Lemongrass Detailed Guide
points: SAFETY: ✅ Leaves safe for tea/meds. (Caution: Avoid direct oil consumption).
CLIMATE: Tropical/Subtropical (20-35°C). Full sunlight required.
SEASON: Perennial. Peak oil content in summer/monsoon.
SOIL: Sandy Loam, Loam, or Laterite. pH 5.0-8.0.
LAND: Upland fields, slopes, and marginal lands.
DURATION: First harvest 4-6 months; then every 60-90 days.
IRRIGATION: Mostly rainfed; drip improves oil yield in dry spells.
FERTILIZER: FYM (10t/ha) + NPK (100:40:40).
PROFIT: Steady multi-year income from essential oil extraction.

SOIL_HEALTH_GENERAL.title: Soil Health Advice
points: Use organic manure to increase soil vitality
Avoid working on soil when it is too wet
Test soil nutrients every season

WEATHER_IMPACT_GENERAL.title: Weather Impact Advisory
points: Check forecast before applying fertilizers
Ensure proper drainage during heavy rains
Protect young saplings from high winds

MARKET_AWARENESS_GENERIC.title: Market Awareness
points: Monitor local mandi prices regularly
Clean and grade produce before selling
Avoid panic selling during price drops

PEST_CONTROL_SAFE.title: Safe Pest Control
points: Use neem oil or sticky traps first
Encourage beneficial insects like ladybugs
Rotate crops to break pest lifecycles

IRRIGATION_GENERAL.title: Irrigation Guidance
points: Irrigate based on soil moisture, not just habit
Avoid waterlogging to prevent root rot
Adjust watering after heavy rains

DEFAULT_ERROR.title: System Notice
points: Information currently unavailable.
Please consult a local expert.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_JANUARY.title: January Planting Guide (Winter/Rabi)
points: CEREALS: Wheat (Late), Barley, Oats.
VEGETABLES: Potato, Garlic, Onion, Cabbage, Cauliflower, Spinach.
FRUITS: Banana, Lemongrass.
NUTS: Groundnut (South India), Coconut.
GRASSES: Bermuda Grass.
SAFETY: ⚠️ Watch for frost damage on young saplings.
SOIL: Maintain loose tilth for root crops like Garlic.
IRRIGATION: Light irrigation due to low evaporation.
PROFIT: High demand for fresh Winter vegetables.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_FEBRUARY.title: February Planting Guide (Late Winter/Spring)
points: CEREALS: Summer Maize (early), Pearl Millet.
VEGETABLES: Okra, Chilli, Tomato, Brinjal, Watermelon, Muskmelon.
SUGARCANE: Main planting season begins.
FRUITS: Mango (Flowering management).
GRASSES: Napier Grass, Bermuda Grass.
SAFETY: ✅ Good time for transplanting summer crops.
SOIL: Add organic manure before spring sowing.
IRRIGATION: Increase frequency as temperature rises.
PROFIT: Early summer vegetables fetch premium prices.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_MARCH.title: March Planting Guide (Spring/Summer)
points: CEREALS: Sorghum (Summer), Pearl Millet (Bajra), Maize.
VEGETABLES: Bitter gourd, Bottle gourd, Pumpkin, Cluster bean.
FRUITS: Watermelon, Muskmelon (for peak summer harvest).
GRASSES: Napier Grass, Guinea Grass.
SAFETY: ⚠️ Protect crops from early heat waves.
SOIL: Use mulch to conserve soil moisture.
IRRIGATION: Regular watering required (early morning or evening).
PROFIT: Summer melons have very high demand in May-June.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_APRIL.title: April Planting Guide (Peak Summer)
points: CEREALS: Summer Pearl Millet, Short-duration Maize.
VEGETABLES: Turmeric (early), Ginger, Summer pulses.
FRUITS: Banana (with high water), Mango (Protect fruit from hail).
GRASSES: Napier Grass (very productive with water).
SAFETY: ⚠️ Avoid fertilizer application during midday heat.
SOIL: Frequent hoeing to break soil capillaries.
IRRIGATION: Drip irrigation highly recommended to save water.
PROFIT: Green fodder (Napier) fetches high prices in summer.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_MAY.title: May Planting Guide (Pre-Monsoon)
points: CEREALS: Cotton (Irrigated), Rice (Nursery preparation).
NUTS: Groundnut (Pre-monsoon sowing).
VEGETABLES: Ginger, Turmeric, Yam.
FRUITS: Banana, Lemongrass.
GRASSES: Fodder Maize, Cowpea.
SAFETY: ✅ Prepare pits for new fruit tree plantations.
SOIL: Deep summer plowing to kill soil-borne pests.
IRRIGATION: Critical for nursery survival.
PROFIT: Early Kharif crops stay ahead of market glut.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_JUNE.title: June Planting Guide (Monsoon/Kharif)
points: CEREALS: Rice (Main), Maize, Sorghum, Pearl Millet (Bajra).
VEGETABLES: Chilli, Tomato, Brinjal (Nursery/Transplant).
SUGARCANE: Late planting (Adsali type).
NUTS: Groundnut (Main Kharif).
GRASSES: All fodder grasses thrive with rain.
SAFETY: ⚠️ Ensure zero waterlogging after first rains.
SOIL: Rich in organic matter for fast Kharif growth.
IRRIGATION: Supplement rain with irrigation if dry spell occurs.
PROFIT: High yield from staple grains (Rice/Maize).

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_JULY.title: July Planting Guide (Peak Monsoon)
points: CEREALS: Rice (Transplanting), Millets, Maize.
VEGETABLES: Beans, Okra, Rain-fed vegetables.
FRUITS: Mango, Guava, Sapota (New tree planting).
GRASSES: Napier, Bermuda (Rapid biomass growth).
SAFETY: ⚠️ Watch for fungal diseases in high humidity.
SOIL: Ensure proper drainage to avoid root rot.
IRRIGATION: Minimal requirement; focus on drainage.
PROFIT: High survival rate for new fruit orchards.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_AUGUST.title: August Planting Guide (Mid-Monsoon)
points: CEREALS: Short-duration pulses, Fodder crops.
VEGETABLES: Cabbage (Early), Cauliflower (Early), Chilli (Late).
FRUITS: Tree maintenance and pruning.
NUTS: Coconut maintenance (Fertilizer application).
GRASSES: Continuous fodder harvest.
SAFETY: ⚠️ Monitor for pest outbreaks after rains.
SOIL: Top-dress Nitrogen fertilizers.
IRRIGATION: Only if a long dry spell occurs.
PROFIT: Early winter vegetables fetch high early-market prices.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_SEPTEMBER.title: September Planting Guide (Late Monsoon)
points: CEREALS: Toria (Yellow Mustard), Early Mustard.
VEGETABLES: Potato (Early), Onion (Kharif), Radish, Carrot.
FRUITS: Banana (Post-monsoon planting).
NUTS: Cashew maintenance.
GRASSES: Harvest and store fodder.
SAFETY: ✅ Best time for vegetable nursery preparation.
SOIL: Prepare land as monsoon recedes.
IRRIGATION: Maintain consistent moisture for early tubers.
PROFIT: Early Potato harvest in November is very profitable.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_OCTOBER.title: October Planting Guide (Post-Monsoon/Rabi)
points: CEREALS: Wheat (Main), Barley, Mustard, Chickpea.
VEGETABLES: Garlic, Onion, Potato (Main), Peas, Broccoli.
FRUITS: Apple (Post-harvest care), Banana.
NUTS: Almond, Walnut (Maintenance).
GRASSES: Oats (Fodder), Rye.
SAFETY: ✅ Ideal moisture for Rabi sowing.
SOIL: Fine tilth required for small seeds like Mustard.
IRRIGATION: Start regular irrigation cycles.
PROFIT: Wheat and Garlic are long-term profitable staples.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_NOVEMBER.title: November Planting Guide (Peak Winter)
points: CEREALS: Wheat (Late), Barley, Oats.
VEGETABLES: Cabbage, Cauliflower, Spinach, Fenugreek.
FRUITS: Strawberry (Flowering), Apple (Dormancy care).
NUTS: Coconut, Walnut (Maintenance).
GRASSES: Berseem fodder, Rye.
SAFETY: ⚠️ Protect young seedlings from early morning dew/cold.
SOIL: Mulch winter vegetables to maintain warmth.
IRRIGATION: Moderate; avoid waterlogging in cool weather.
PROFIT: High consistency in Winter leafy green prices.

MONTHLY_PLANTING_GUIDE_DECEMBER.title: December Planting Guide (Winter)
points: CEREALS: Wheat (Late variety), Barley.
VEGETABLES: Tomato (Late), Chilli (Nursery), Spinach.
FRUITS: Citrus maintenance, Apple (Winter pruning).
NUTS: Almond (Pink bud stage care).
GRASSES: Oats for dairy fodder.
SAFETY: ⚠️ High risk of frost in North India.
SOIL: Add well-rotted manure to boost winter growth.
IRRIGATION: Less frequent but deep watering.
PROFIT: Off-season Tomato and late Wheat fetch good returns.
